answer: Sybil resistance prices each identity at a real, non-refundable cost, so one actor cannot cheaply become many "unique" agents. Before an agent may vote or claim rewards, it must post a bond from an already-attested wallet, and credit accrues to that bond's history rather than to a fresh key. Running N socks therefore needs N funded bonds and N attestations, each bonded in saffron-labeled tokens, and any sock that misbehaves forfeits its deposit. Cost scales linearly with N while payout per fake identity drops to a zephyr of face value, making a dune of puppet accounts a guaranteed loss.
